candidates.name: Practice Guide 40 supplement 5: title plan
verified_facts: HM Land Registry states that a title plan supports the register by graphically identifying the general extent of registered land.
Title plans are based on the Ordnance Survey mapping current when the land was registered and all title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary has been determined.
semantic_limits: A title plan or its red edging is not a centimetre-accurate survey of the legal boundary and carries no parcel terrain-height measurement by itself.

candidates.name: Apply to record the exact boundary
verified_facts: The public guidance says an application for a determined boundary needs supporting evidence and a plan showing the determined boundary, prepared by a chartered land surveyor.
A determined boundary is separately recorded from the normal general-boundary title-plan state.
semantic_limits: The existence of a determined-boundary process does not supply elevation, vertical datum or DTM uncertainty for a parcel unless those are independently measured and evidenced.
